title: Keep nonmetal AIT at least 100 K above use temperature
evidence_basis: Prefer nonmetallic materials whose ASTM G72 autogenous ignition temperature exceeds maximum use temperature by at least 100 K.

title: Minimize dead-ends, cavities, and contaminant traps
evidence_basis: Blind passages, drill points, and dead-end cavities accumulate debris and create ignition-prone geometries.

source.section: Design for Cleanliness and Maintaining Cleanliness

title: Design for cleaning and clean maintenance
evidence_basis: Systems should be easy to disassemble, thoroughly clean, and maintain in a clean condition.

source.section: Design for Cleanliness and Maintaining Cleanliness

title: Use slow-opening bypass equalization
evidence_basis: Compatible bypass valves allow controlled pressure equalization and reduce particle-impact and heat-of-compression risk.

source.section: Design for Cleanliness and Maintaining Cleanliness

title: Install filters at oxygen entry and upstream of high-velocity hardware
evidence_basis: Recommended filter locations include oxygen entry points, disconnect points, and upstream of valves, regulators, and other high-velocity-producing components.

source.section: Design for Cleanliness and Maintaining Cleanliness

title: Use the finest practical filtration
evidence_basis: Use the smallest filtration that still meets flow requirements and cleanliness targets to reduce particle burden.

source.section: Design for Cleanliness and Maintaining Cleanliness

title: Use burn-resistant filter media
evidence_basis: Filter elements have high surface-area-to-volume ratios and should be made from burn-resistant materials.

source.section: Design for Cleanliness and Maintaining Cleanliness

title: Purge with filtered dry inert gas after assembly
evidence_basis: After assembly, purge with clean, dry, oil-free filtered inert gas to remove assembly-generated contaminants.

source.section: Design for Cleanliness and Maintaining Cleanliness

title: Minimize particulate generation in operation and maintenance
evidence_basis: Use bearings, bushings, and configurations that keep generated particulate away from oxygen-wetted regions.

source.section: Design for Cleanliness and Maintaining Cleanliness

title: Protect vent line terminations from contamination
evidence_basis: Vent terminations should be protected using tees, screens, or equivalent measures to prevent contaminants, insects, and animals from entering the system.

source.section: Design for Cleanliness and Maintaining Cleanliness

title: Keep GOX velocity below about 30.5 m/s where practical
evidence_basis: Gas velocities above approximately 30.5 m/s (100 ft/s) should receive special attention, especially at restrictions.

title: Use burn-resistant alloys downstream of high-velocity disturbances
evidence_basis: Traditional practice is to use burn-resistant alloys for at least eight to ten pipe diameters downstream of throttling disturbances.

title: Avoid nonmetals where sonic velocity can occur
evidence_basis: Where sonic velocity cannot be avoided, use ignition-resistant materials and keep nonmetals out of those locations.

title: Blow down with filtered dry nitrogen before oxygen service
evidence_basis: Maintain cleanliness and perform blowdown with filtered dry gaseous nitrogen at maximum anticipated pressure and flow before wetting with oxygen.

title: Use long-radius bends instead of sharp bends
evidence_basis: Long-radius bends reduce the likelihood of particle impingement.

title: Prefer nonrotating stems, grounded internals, and manual bypass valves
evidence_basis: Nonrotating stems reduce particulate generation and galling; bypass valves reduce pressure-surge risk; electrical grounding reduces static accumulation.
